criteria.criterion: A function in crates/athena-core (reading consistency check) returns an error naming the file when a criterion that restricts the change to named files omits a deliverable path, or when a deliverables list contains CHANGELOG.md while a criterion excludes it.
criteria.evidence: `check_scope_consistency` in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs returns an Err that names the omitted deliverable path, or names CHANGELOG.md when a criterion leaves it out. Checked by reading the diff.

criteria.criterion: build_reading in crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs calls the check after the deliverables are normalized, so a contradictory reading is rejected before it is recorded or shown; admission.rs also calls it on the accepted reading.
criteria.evidence: reading.rs:608 calls the check after the normalize_path loop (lines 538-555) and after validate(). An Err makes the reader's output invalid (lines 460-464). admission.rs pushes a `reading-scope` violation when the check fails.

criteria.criterion: defaults.toml gains a `changelog` default, applying to code, tests, docs, config, build and prompts, which says every change adds a CHANGELOG.md entry; defaults.toml is named in this criterion as an intended change.
criteria.evidence: defaults.toml adds id="changelog" with applies_to [code, tests, docs, config, build, prompts] and the statement "Every change adds a CHANGELOG.md entry...". A test in defaults.rs asserts this.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md tells the reader to list CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable and to keep file-scope criteria consistent with the deliverables list.
criteria.evidence: The prompt gains two new lines: "list CHANGELOG.md as a deliverable; never exclude it" and "A criterion saying only some files change must name every deliverable and no other file, or Athena rejects the reading."

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md gains an entry for this change.
criteria.evidence: There are two new bullets under ### Fixed in CHANGELOG.md.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` and confirm the new unit tests pass: consistent scope accepted, scope omitting a deliverable rejected, scope excluding CHANGELOG.md while it is listed rejected, and a reading with no scope criterion accepted.
criteria.evidence: The scoped run shows all 5 new reading tests pass, covering the four required cases plus the out-of-list file case. The full run finished; Athena reports 384 tests passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`; both are clean.
criteria.evidence: clippy finished with no warnings, and fmt --check produced no output.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG exclusion check runs on every criterion and matches very loose words, so it rejects ordinary consistent readings, including this job's own accepted reading.
findings.evidence: Found by reading the code; I could not run it because I may not write files. When CHANGELOG.md is a deliverable, every criterion (not just file-scope ones) is rejected if "not ", "exclud", "without" or "never" appears within 40 characters before "changelog", or "exclud" or "unchanged" appears within 40 after. This job's accepted criterion 1 ("...contains CHANGELOG.md while a criterion excludes it.") has "exclud" in the after-window. Its criterion 6 ("scope excluding CHANGELOG.md while it is listed rejected") has "exclud" in the before-window. So build_reading would have rejected this very reading. A plain criterion such as "The command does not panic, and CHANGELOG.md gains an entry" is rejected too. A rejection makes the reader's output invalid and yields no reading (reading.rs:460-464); the code shows no re-prompt. Admission would flag the same readings as `reading-scope` violations. This swaps the old failure mode for new false-positive job failures, against the request's goal. The heuristic should be limited to file-scope criteria or to tighter negation patterns.

The tests cover only the four required cases. None checks that a criterion which mentions CHANGELOG.md near an unrelated negation, or describes the rule, is accepted. That is how the major finding above went unnoticed.

findings.summary: The reader prompt was reworded beyond the two new lines.
findings.evidence: Every bullet and the forecasts section were shortened. docs/decisions.md D89 says this was done to stay within the reader prompt budget. Meaning looks preserved, but it widens the diff.

summary: Verdict: fail. Every acceptance criterion is met, but the new check rejects this job's own accepted reading. The change adds `check_scope_consistency`, called from build_reading and from admission, plus a `changelog` default, the reader prompt lines, a changelog entry and decision D89. The new tests pass, and clippy and fmt are clean. The failure comes from the CHANGELOG half of the check: it runs on every criterion, not just file-scope ones, and treats words like "not", "never", "without" or "exclud" within 40 characters of "changelog" as excluding it. Criteria 1 and 6 of this job's reading would both be rejected, and so would ordinary criteria like "does not panic, and CHANGELOG.md gains an entry". A rejected reading produces no reading, with no re-prompt that I could see in the code. That swaps the old failures for new false rejections, so I rate it major. I found this by reading the code and could not run it, because I may not write files. The fix: apply the exclusion test only to file-scope criteria or to tight negation patterns, and add tests for consistent wordings that should be accepted.
